title: Director of Procurement & Trading
descriptionHtml:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

The Role

This is not a traditional procurement role. At Andercore, procurement is trading: fast-paced, market-driven, and executed daily — not on quarterly or annual cycles. You will lead a team of young and hungry category managers, through high-volume purchasing decisions in a dynamic environment where prices, availability, and supplier landscapes shift constantly.

You will own end-to-end procurement strategy and execution: sourcing, onboarding to the system, supplier negotiations and disputes, pricing, team leadership, and process design. We need someone who can think strategically and execute operationally every single day — from setting category strategy to approving individual purchase orders. You will be in the driver seat to build the first AI automated trading engine - a unique opportunity in the industrial supply space.

You report directly to the C level and sit on the commercial and operations leadership team. Andercore uses AI extensively across the business; you will be expected to leverage it to drive efficiency, margins, and scalability in procurement.

The core purpose of this role is to build one buying strategy that combines three things:

  • Spot trading, run as a repeatable system with a regular market-coverage schedule and clear KPIs;

  • Strategic buying, where you negotiate allocations, framework agreements and terms with Tier-1 manufacturers and develop private-label and direct-from-factory categories;

  • Supply planning, where you set the mix of spot, contract and stock and keep price and inventory risk under control.

Each part on its own is not enough. The job is to make them work together so that Andercore buys at the right price, secures supply when the market tightens, and never holds stock it cannot sell.

What You Will Do

  • Build and run the procurement machine: Develop and execute procurement strategies that support an 8-digit monthly procurement spend with exponential growth. Negotiate favourable terms, pricing, and contracts with suppliers on a daily basis.

  • Lead and develop the team: Manage 10+ team members, set clear priorities daily, coach emerging team leads, and create a culture of accountability and speed. You will need to be assertive and hands-on. Be the player-coach. Close deals yourself and hire the people you need to scale

  • Create scalable processes: Design, implement, and continuously improve procurement workflows, playbooks, and controls. Processes are implemented in days and weeks at Andercore — not quarters and years.

  • Own supplier relationships: Source, evaluate, and onboard suppliers. Maintain and expand a high-quality supplier network with strong retention across existing and emerging markets.

  • Drive margin improvement: Identify cost-saving opportunities, optimise purchasing decisions, and improve payment terms to boost net revenue margin and cash cycle.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Logistics, Accounting, and Product & Engineering to align supply with demand and ensure operational excellence.

  • Full P&L responsibility: for the supply side.

  • Leverage data and AI: Use data to inform purchasing decisions, monitor supplier performance, and identify market trends. Embrace AI tools to automate and scale procurement operations.

  • AI-native procurement: automate processes from RFQs through to order confirmations, with sellers as co-designers of the agents.

What Success Looks Like

  • Revenue and margin targets consistently met or exceeded through high availability and competitive pricing.

  • A robust, high-quality supplier network with strong retention and engagement across existing and emerging markets.

  • Streamlined, repeatable processes that reduce time-to-onboard, minimise errors, and allow the team to scale without linear headcount growth.

  • A high-performing, motivated team with emerging team leads and strong cross-functional collaboration.

  • Accurate, data-driven reporting that drives continuous improvement and informs executive strategy.

  • Run a category management that unlocks and owns new product lines

Who You Are

Must-Haves

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree from a top university or business school.

  • 4+ years in a high-performance environment: for example commodity trading / high-velocity B2B procurement.

  • Proven ability to build processes and delegate effectively. You must be able to create systems that outlast your personal involvement — not do everything yourself.

  • Strong assertiveness and people leadership. You will manage a young team that needs clear direction, daily prioritisation, and coaching.

  • Ability to operate at both strategic and granular levels: setting category strategy in the morning and reviewing individual POs in the afternoon.

  • Excellent analytical and communication skills.

  • Fluent English is required; German is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable with a high-intensity, fast-paced startup environment where priorities can shift daily.

  • Proven results negotiating from the smaller side of the table, i.e. securing allocation, pricing and terms when you are not the biggest customer.

  • Hard-working, proactive, and independent. Willing to go the extra mile to get the job done.

  • A personal track record in spot or commodity trading with margin ownership.

  • Experience scaling a team, plus forecasting and inventory risk management.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in marketplaces, SaaS, or construction / infrastructure / energy materials.

  • Exposure to AI-driven operations or automation of procurement workflows.

  • Familiarity with cross-border trade and international supplier management.

  • Tier-1 strategy consulting background (e.g. McKinsey, BCG, Bain).

This Role Is Not For You If…

  • Your procurement experience is in slow-cycle, enterprise purchasing (annual contracts, quarterly reviews). Our cadence is daily.

  • You are strong on analysis but weak on implementation. We need someone who executes, not just diagnoses.

  • You prefer to do things yourself rather than build teams and processes. Delegation and system-building are non-negotiable.

  • You need a fully structured environment to be effective. Here, you will create the structure.

What We Offer

  • A critical leadership role with direct impact on company growth and P&L.

  • Highly competitive compensation with performance-based incentives.

  • A smart, ambitious team backed by top-tier investors — building something that doesn’t exist yet.

  • Berlin headquarters with a global, multicultural operating environment.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.

title: Director Solutions (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Director Solutions (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites in Europe and the US · Reports to the CEO · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

A robot deal is won twice: once when the contract is signed, and once when the cell runs the customer’s orders at the throughput we promised. The distance between the two is decided before anyone unpacks a crate: by the site survey, the item spectrum, the cell concept, the integration with the customer’s warehouse systems, and by the number we write into the contract.

We are moving from single stations to fleets, with customers who order dozens of systems at once. The deals are getting larger, the sites more varied, and a concept that does not fit the site is paid for in months of commissioning. We are looking for the technical counterpart to our sales team: a leader who sits next to every account executive from the first conversation and makes deals technically feasible. Someone who has deployed robots personally, knows what a real site does to a design, finds the solution that makes the customer’s use case work, and makes sure what we promise is what we can build.

The Real-World Learning Loop starts with your design

Cortex learns from live deployments. The cell you design is the body the model works in, and a concept that goes live in weeks instead of months is weeks of real-world data no one else has.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every station runs the current policy on the customer’s items. Your surface on it: reach, camera placement and item presentation that let the policy do its job on day one.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: standard cells with a known stack wherever possible, so every pick teaches the same model.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: the item spectrum and the sample tests you run before signature, so curation starts before go-live.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies return to the fleet after validation. Your surface on it: concepts that transfer, so a policy proven on one cell works on the next.

A site designed right goes live faster, teaches Cortex more, and grows.

Responsibilities

  • Be Sales’ technical counterpart on every deal. One solutions lead next to every account executive, from the first customer conversation to signature. Your job is to make the deal technically feasible: understand the customer’s process, find the solution that works for their site and items, and give Sales a technical story the customer’s engineers believe.

  • Own the technical solution for every deal, from the first site visit to the signed scope: site survey, process and material-flow analysis, item spectrum, cell concept and layout, reach and camera study, integration concept for WMS, WCS and conveyors, safety concept. One package per deal, and you are accountable for it.

  • Set the number. Throughput, pick success and intervention rates we commit to per site, derived from the item spectrum and the site and checked against what comparable live sites actually do. No KPI goes into a contract without your sign-off.

  • Standard first. Configure our standard single-arm, dual-arm and mobile products to the site. Every deviation is a documented decision taken with Engineering, not a discovery during installation.

  • Run the gate. No contract is signed without your solution design sign-off and a delivery slot agreed with Operations. You hold the pen on the technical statement of work, the acceptance criteria and the site-readiness list the customer has to meet.

  • Make it feasible, fast. Sample tests, pick studies and scanning or dimensioning checks with our applied AI team, within days, not months. When a requirement does not fit, find the version that does: a different cell or item presentation, a phased scope, a pilot that proves the hard part first. A no is the last answer, not the first.

  • Hand over to Deployment a package that builds: layout, configuration, integration spec, acceptance criteria, risks and dates, so commissioning executes without reopening the concept. You stay accountable until the first live orders prove the design.

  • Own the interfaces to integrators and WMS vendors at the solution level, from AutoStore and goods-to-person systems to conveyor and WMS partners: interface specs, a clear split of responsibilities and readiness tests before we ship.

  • Build the solution library: reference designs per use case (goods-to-person ports, put walls, returns, decanting, store replenishment), throughput models, layout templates and integration patterns, so the tenth deal of a kind takes a day, not a month.

  • Close the loop from the field. What commissioning and live sites learn about a design flows back into the reference concepts and into requirements for Product and Engineering.

  • Lead the big pursuits in person: the technical counterpart to the customer’s engineering and operations teams in fleet deals, tenders and RFPs; demos and reference visits with the customer’s real items.

  • Build and lead the Solutions team in Europe and the US: solutions engineers who have stood at a cell, with the playbooks and tools (CAD, simulation, throughput models) to do this at ten times today’s deal flow.

  • Partner with Sales, Operations and Deployment, Service Accounts, Systems Engineering, Applied AI and Supply Chain. Report to the CEO and be part of the leadership team.

Not in scope, by design

  • Pricing, contract terms and closing stay with Sales. You are their technical counterpart: you own what we promise technically, how we make it work and when it can be delivered.

  • Build, installation and commissioning up to the Site Acceptance Test stay with Operations. You hand over a package that builds, and you stay accountable for the concept.

  • Live sites after acceptance stay with Service Accounts. You design for the site they will have to run.

  • Product and system design stay with Engineering and New Product Introduction. You configure the standard; what the standard lacks, you bring them as requirements.

What makes this role hard

  • Your job is to find the yes we can deliver. Most of the time that means a smarter solution, sometimes a different scope or a later date, and occasionally a no to a deal the company wants. When it is a no, you have to be right about it, with numbers.

  • The product moves fast: what the model could not do in spring it may do in autumn. You commit to today’s capability and plan for tomorrow’s, and you do not confuse the two.

  • The site is never finished. WMS, conveyors, bins and item master data belong to the customer or an integrator, and your design has to survive their reality.

  • Every shortcut in the concept comes back as months of commissioning. You carry both sides of that trade, in front of Sales and in front of Deployment.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: every open deal has a solution package and a realistic commitment; the gate is in place (checklist, sign-off, delivery slot); every live site’s concept reviewed for what we would design differently today.

  • By month 6: reference designs for our three main use cases; a throughput model validated against live sites; interface specifications agreed with our three most important integration partners; the first solutions engineer in the US onboarded.

  • By month 12: deals signed in 2027 go live at the throughput in the concept, without redesign; a Solutions team in Europe and the US; a library that makes the standard deal routine.

What you bring

  • 8+ years in warehouse or factory automation, several of them in solutions, application engineering or deployment of robotic systems. You have personally deployed robots in live operations, from site survey to commissioning: piece-picking arms, dual-arm cells, mobile manipulators or AMR fleets. You know what a go-live night feels like.

Conversations with the founders and our VP Operations, a working session on a real site (we give you a layout, an item spectrum and a target; you tell us what to build and what to promise), and time with the team in Stuttgart. We move fast.

title: Dispenser
descriptionHtml:
About Bolt Pharmacy and AIOS

AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.

We’re at $450M ARR, growing from $7M/yr in April 2025. We’re faithfully serving >200k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’ve just launched Bolt Med, our international brand. We’re profitable.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

  1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.

  2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Since April 2025 we've grown from 3k to 200k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2030: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: Working at AIOS

Being a Dispenser at Bolt Pharmacy

We are building a world-class team.

As a Dispenser at Bolt Pharmacy (part of AIOS), your fundamental role is to turn prescriptions into treatment patients can count on - safely, accurately and at pace.

You'll be at the heart of our dispensing operation, selecting, labelling and securely packing medicines for patients across the UK. You'll take ownership of your work within your qualified scope, follow dispensing procedures precisely and escalate clinical questions to our pharmacists. Every prescription has a person behind it.

You'll keep quality high as volumes grow. From protecting the cold chain and monitoring storage temperatures to managing stock and checking deliveries, you'll help keep medicines safe and orders moving. You'll report errors and near misses promptly, so we learn quickly and keep improving.

Working alongside pharmacists, fellow dispensers and our stock and customer service teams, you'll help resolve issues before they delay treatment. You'll also support trainee dispensers and spot practical ways to make Bolt Pharmacy's operation more efficient. Your experience will help raise the standard of the whole team.

Great performance means consistently processing 30+ orders per hour while maintaining over 99.5% dispensing accuracy, zero critical errors and full compliance with our procedures. Patients receive the right treatment, colleagues trust your work and we can serve more people with confidence.

This is a full-time, on-site role at Bolt Pharmacy in Blackburn, UK, working standard business hours with possible shift patterns.

You'll report directly to our Shift Lead and work closely with our Site Operations Lead, Michal Binkowski.

You'll work most closely with Bolt Pharmacy's pharmacists, qualified and trainee dispensers, Stock Control and Customer Service, combining dispensing oversight, shared workloads and patient support.

Key responsibilities

  • Get every prescription right: Select, label and prepare medicines accurately within your qualified scope, following SOPs and escalating clinical queries to pharmacists.

  • Keep treatment moving: Process and securely pack 30+ orders per hour while maintaining accuracy, safety and compliance.

  • Protect every medicine: Maintain cold-chain controls, monitor fridge and room temperatures, and escalate storage deviations immediately.

  • Take ownership of stock: Check incoming deliveries, maintain correct storage and rotation, and support stock takes so medicines are available when needed.

  • Make quality everyone's business: Record errors, near misses and incidents promptly, keep workstations clean and compliant, follow hygiene and PPE procedures, and suggest practical improvements.

  • Raise the team's standard: Guide trainee dispensers, support colleagues and work with Customer Service to resolve patient queries and order updates.

Need to have

  • Dispensing qualification: You hold a valid Buttercups certification or equivalent dispensing qualification.

  • Experience at pace: You've worked in high-volume dispensing and can consistently meet a target of 30+ orders per hour without compromising safety.

  • Attention to detail: You bring exceptional accuracy to medicine selection, labelling and prescription preparation.

  • Ownership within your scope: You organise your workload independently, follow SOPs precisely and know when to involve a pharmacist.

  • Professionalism: You're reliable, punctual and committed to patient safety and regulatory compliance.

Nice to have

  • Qualified experience: You've spent at least a year working as a qualified dispenser.

  • Online pharmacy: You understand the demands of dispensing and dispatching treatment to patients remotely.

  • Mentoring: You've trained or supported junior colleagues and can explain procedures clearly.

  • Stock management: You bring experience in inventory control, stock rotation and keeping a busy dispensary supplied.

  • Patient support: You've handled healthcare queries with care, clarity and professionalism.

  • Pharmacy standards: You're familiar with GPhC requirements and how they translate into everyday practice.

Our cultural standards

We aim to make this your life's work. This should be the most challenging, most rewarding role of your life. Accordingly, these are the core cultural standards to which we hold ourselves & our team-members:

  1. Belief in the mission: We will have served 100 million patients by the end of 2035 and we transform the life of most patients who join. We have a lot of work to do. We are obsessed with our patients and are dedicated to the mission.

  2. Unwavering integrity: We are at the frontier, so we often live in ambiguity with no trodden path. When we can't look to others for guidance, we must maintain impeccable ethics and unwavering integrity.

  3. Only the paranoid survive: Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you're choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we've already done, however far we've already come — it's still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

  4. If we're average we fail: We are only interested in "insanely great", a focus on the quality of our execution that in everyday life would be considered pathological. We have a dedication to excellence and reject incompetence.

  5. Commitment to candor: That which can be destroyed by the truth should be. You get full transparency from the company and the company expects full transparency from you. We never say anything about someone that we wouldn't say to them directly. We give feedback with love and do not need to protect people from fleeting physical sensations.

  6. A maniacal sense of urgency: We execute at an intensity that most people think is impossible. Speed is critical and we need things done yesterday. We all work very hard and in such a competitive world there really is no other way to win.

  7. Enduring frugality: We are frugal. We hate being wasteful and we are anti-luxury. A culture of cheapness keeps us young. We spend our cash wisely & carefully — in a way that would make our grandmas proud.

  8. Bulldozing barriers: The world is malleable and we shape it. We truly believe this and act accordingly. We are relentlessly resourceful and are at the mercy of no-one but ourselves. You'll be shocked how capable you are and how much you can achieve.

  9. Keep your head down: We're boring people doing exciting work. We don't chase short-term status — we ignore short-term dopamine hits and focus on what matters. Outsiders will underestimate us and we revel in that.

  10. The power of focus: We live in a world of power laws and we cannot overestimate the unimportance of practically everything. Know your One Thing, and nail it.

🎯 "You just build a f*ing amazing experience. Make each step amazing. Make every decision in the long term interest of the customer. Give the customer massively more value than you take."

Compensation & Benefits

Our compensation package includes equity, giving you the opportunity to share in what we build.

  • Training role: £13 per hour while you complete the required training and sign-off.

  • Qualified role: £15 per hour in total compensation, including equity, once you have completed the required training and are qualified and signed off for the role.

Benefits

The stuff below is cool as well.

  • Personal development: A £400 budget for books, courses and coaching to keep building your skills.

  • Personal wellness: A £400 budget for the gym and health apps to support your wellbeing.

  • GLP-1s: Get free membership with a clinic offering GLP-1s, if clinically applicable.

  • Health coaching: Access free biweekly health coaching to help you stay healthy.

  • Work coaching: Access free biweekly work coaching to stay sharp and calm.

  • What are we missing? We're still early, so your ideas can help shape our culture.

At Oxa, we're building the future of Industrial Mobile Autonomy (IMA) and are in the market for new talent.

Oxa’s customers are the operators of some of the world's largest industrial facilities. Our technology transforms existing industrial vehicles into intelligent autonomous fleets, unlocking new levels of productivity, safety, and performance.

 

‘The phone in your hand, the coffee on your desk, the shirt on your back - they all moved through a web of ports (air and sea), distribution yards and manufacturing hubs. This is the invisible circulatory system of global trade, and it relies entirely on a relentless, repetitive shuffle of goods. Towing.

This towing task happens in complex, commerce-critical industrial environments. Here, having self driving technology “do the driving” delivers immediate, measurable impact. IMA will revolutionise the movement of goods across the world's ports, airports, and yards.

You can be part of that as an Oxbot’

‘Paul Newman - Founder and CEO’

 

Our Products:

Our products are built on four core technology pillars which come together to build a complete system:

Oxa Ware – Our modular autonomy hardware systems for consistent and repeatable integration of autonomy with existing vehicles.

Oxa Driver – Our Physical AI, embodied in Oxa Ware, self-driving software that enables vehicles to perceive, reason, and drive autonomously in complex real-world environments.

Oxa Foundry – Our development toolchain that leverages generative AI to continuously train and assure Oxa Driver, synthesising situations and sensor data.

Oxa Hub – Our suite of cloud services for monitoring, managing and orchestrating fleets driven by Oxa Driver, including an API for integration with existing logistics systems.

 

Behind these technologies is our exceptional team, the Oxbots. We are home to some of the world's leading experts in autonomous systems, robotics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, and distributed software engineering. Together, we're solving some of the hardest technical challenges in autonomy, turning the research and development we do into production and deploying it into environments. Making robots do useful work.

Your Role:

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer and Wireman possessing recent exposure to working within an automotive environment to build, assemble, and test wiring harnesses, complete SMT PCB assembly, and offer practical support throughout the lifecycle of intricate loom projects. The Engineer will also assist in troubleshooting power, network, and CAN diagnostic issues on active vehicles.

Requirements:

  • Core Portfolio: Track record of building complex sensor looms and functional wiring harness projects.

title: Elektroniker oder Elektrokonstrukteur (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Dein Job für sauberere Luft. Werde Emission Partner.

Technik aus dem Saterland. Wirkung weit darüber hinaus.

In der Gemeinde Saterland entwickeln und produzieren wir Technologien, die Schadstoffemissionen reduzieren. Unsere Katalysatoren und Systeme kommen dort zum Einsatz, wo Abgase zuverlässig gereinigt und Emissionsgrenzwerte eingehalten werden müssen.

Moderne Abgasnachbehandlung braucht dabei mehr als einen leistungsfähigen Katalysator. Elektronik, Automatisierung und eine durchdachte Anlagensteuerung sorgen dafür, dass unsere Systeme zuverlässig arbeiten und Emissionen gezielt reduziert werden können.

Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Als Elektroniker oder Elektrokonstrukteur arbeitest du an der elektrotechnischen Auslegung unserer Sonderanlagen. Du projektierst elektrische Komponenten, erstellst Schalt- und Stromlaufpläne und sorgst gemeinsam mit Mechanik, Fluidtechnik und Software dafür, dass aus einzelnen Komponenten eine funktionierende Anlage entsteht.

Du möchtest Elektrotechnik nicht nur nach Plan umsetzen, sondern technische Lösungen mitgestalten und am Ende sehen, was aus deiner Arbeit entstanden ist? Dann werde Emission Partner.

Was du bei uns bewirkst

Du bringst die Elektronik in unsere Anlagen zur Emissionsminderung.

Bei uns arbeitest du an individuellen Lösungen für die Abgasnachbehandlung. Du begleitest die Elektrotechnik von der ersten Konzeption über die Auswahl und Dimensionierung der Komponenten bis zur Dokumentation.

Dabei arbeitest du eng mit anderen technischen Fachbereichen zusammen. Was du projektierst, bleibt also nicht auf dem Bildschirm oder im Schaltplan: An unserem Standort entstehen daraus reale Anlagen und Systeme.

So sorgst du mit deiner Arbeit dafür, dass unsere Technik zur Emissionsminderung zuverlässig funktioniert.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du übernimmst die Konzeption und Projektierung der Automatisierungs- und Elektrotechnik unserer Sonderanlagen zur Abgasnachbehandlung.
  • Du berechnest und dimensionierst elektrische Komponenten und wählst die passenden Bauteile für unsere Anwendungen aus.
  • Du erstellst Schalt- und Stromlaufpläne, Kabellisten und weitere technische Unterlagen.
  • Du sorgst für eine vollständige und nachvollziehbare elektrotechnische Dokumentation.
  • Du prüfst deine Projektierung im Hinblick auf die relevanten elektrotechnischen Vorschriften und Normen.
  • Du stimmst elektrische Lösungen mit den Bereichen Mechanik, Fluidtechnik und Software ab.
  • Du begleitest deine Projekte von der Planung bis zur praktischen Umsetzung und arbeitest eng mit den Kolleginnen und Kollegen in Entwicklung und Fertigung zusammen.
  • Du bringst deine Erfahrung ein und hilfst uns dabei, unsere Anlagen und elektrotechnischen Lösungen kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.


Das bringst du mit

Uns ist wichtiger, was du kannst und wohin du dich entwickeln möchtest, als ein perfekter Lebenslauf.

  • Du hast eine abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung im elektrotechnischen Bereich, beispielsweise als Elektroniker, Elektriker oder Elektroinstallateur (m/w/d).
  • Du hast ein gutes Verständnis für elektrische und technische Zusammenhänge.
  • Idealerweise bringst du bereits Erfahrung in der Elektrokonstruktion, Projektierung oder im Umgang mit elektrischen Prüfmitteln mit.
  • Du kannst dich in technische Zeichnungen, Schaltpläne und Dokumentationen einarbeiten.
  • Du arbeitest sorgfältig, strukturiert und selbstständig.
  • Du löst technische Fragestellungen gerne gemeinsam mit anderen Fachbereichen.

title: Embedded Automotive Platforms, Staff Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

The Embedded Automotive Platforms (EAP) group builds the software that connects Wayve’s AI Driver to the vehicle and its onboard systems. We develop the platform adaptation and integration layers that let our AI capabilities run reliably across different vehicles, hardware platforms and programmes.

You’ll join a team working across Wayve’s internal fleets and customer programmes. Our work spans embedded software that resides between vehicle platforms, HMI and AI Driver, and the software interfaces that connect these capabilities to the AI Driver. We work closely with teams across autonomy, hardware, product and vehicle engineering to turn system requirements into robust, testable software.

As a Staff Software engineer, you’ll own significant technical work from design through integration and validation. You’ll help shape how EAP software is structured, make sound engineering decisions in an evolving environment, and work with partner teams to deliver capabilities that operate reliably on real vehicles.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Design, build and maintain embedded software that integrates Wayve’s AI Driver with vehicle platforms and onboard systems.

  • Develop and evolve interfaces between AI capabilities, vehicle software and platform-specific components.

  • Work across areas such as inference integration, vehicle data, navigation, localisation, odometry, driver interaction and motion control interfaces.

  • Collaborate with engineers across autonomy, hardware, vehicle programmes and product to clarify requirements and resolve integration issues.

  • Take features from technical design through implementation, testing, vehicle integration and release.

  • Diagnose and resolve issues using simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, vehicle testing, logs and performance data.

  • Contribute to architecture and engineering practices that support reuse across vehicle platforms and programmes.

  • Use AI development tools where they can improve engineering productivity and software quality.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Building and integrating software for current and future vehicle platforms, including internal development fleets and customer programmes.

  • Developing reliable interfaces and adaptation software between Wayve’s AI Driver and vehicle-specific systems.

  • Improving software quality, observability, performance and resilience in resource-constrained onboard environments.

  • Supporting the migration and evolution of capabilities across vehicle generations and hardware configurations.

  • Working with simulation and test teams to improve how embedded and vehicle-integrated software is validated.

  • Contributing to technical direction, reviewing designs and code, and helping raise engineering standards across the team.

🙌 You should apply if

  • Essential: a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical, Automotive Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Essential: strong software engineering experience in modern C++, with a track record of delivering production-quality software.

  • Essential: experience developing embedded or systems software, ideally on Nvidia and Qualcomm platforms with Linux/QNX.

  • Essential: experience with Linux-based platforms.

  • Essential: experience with system architecture and designing software components, APIs or interfaces for complex systems.

  • Essential: strong understanding of software quality practices, including testing, debugging, code review and maintainability.

  • Essential: experience diagnosing problems across component or system boundaries.

  • Essential: ability to work with technical partners to clarify requirements and make progress in ambiguous situations.

  • Essential: clear communication and collaboration skills, including working across teams and locations.

  • Essential: a practical, ownership-minded approach, so you can take a complex problem from investigation through implementation and validation.

  • Desirable: experience in autonomous driving, automotive, robotics or another real-time, safety-related domain.

  • Desirable: familiarity with vehicle software, middleware, sensors, actuators or vehicle communication protocols.

  • Desirable: experience integrating machine-learning inference or other compute-intensive workloads on embedded hardware.

  • Desirable: familiarity with AV stack components like navigation, state estimation or driver-interaction systems.

  • Desirable: experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing or vehicle testing.

  • Desirable: familiarity with automotive software development processes, including ASPICE or similar practices.

  • Desirable: experience supporting software across multiple hardware platforms or vehicle programmes.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency Interviews (Programming and hiring manager interview; 1.5 hours total)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (Systems & domain-specific interviews; 4 hours total)

  • Final interview: Mission & values alignment (30 mins).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Embedded Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Location: Eindhoven, the Netherlands (on-site, High Tech Campus) | Type: Full-time | Level: Medior–Senior, ~5 years of relevant experience

About us

AIM Solutions is an early-stage deep-tech startup in Eindhoven building inspection and metrology equipment for the semiconductor industry. We are in an active build phase: a small, growing team turning lab setups into a tool that does not exist anywhere else yet.

The role

As Embedded Engineer you own everything between the instrument hardware and our acquisition software. You integrate cameras, frame grabbers, motion controllers, piezo stages, lasers and FPGA timing hardware, and you make them run as one synchronized, reliable scan. The work is hands-on: vendor SDKs, trigger wiring, PCIe cards and lab networks one day, clean driver code and a live data stream to the user interface the next. You work closely with the System, Mechatronics, Application and Algorithm engineers.

What you will do

  • Design the trigger and acquisition architecture that synchronizes camera exposure, stage motion and laser pulses.

  • Integrate industrial cameras and frame grabbers through industry-standard interfaces and vendor SDKs, from driver set-up to stable high-rate acquisition.

  • Integrate motion controllers and positioning stages through vendor APIs and controller scripting, including commissioning and tuning with the Mechatronics Engineer.

  • Develop and extend FPGA-based timing and I/O for triggering and position-synchronized acquisition.

  • Write driver and control layers in C/C++ and Python that the scan and reconstruction software builds on, and expose live status and data streams to the user interface.

  • Own the instrument PC and lab network set-up: PCIe hardware, high-speed Ethernet links between devices, IP planning and device discovery.

  • Bring up and debug hardware in the lab with oscilloscope, logic analyzer and network captures, and document interfaces and timing budgets with the System Engineer.

  • Take part in code review and help move the set-up from prototype to a reproducible, maintainable tool.

Your profile

  • MSc in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Applied Physics or a related field.

  • ~5 years of hands-on experience integrating and controlling hardware, preferably in high-tech equipment, scientific instruments or industrial automation.

  • Strong C/C++ and Python, including working with vendor SDKs and drivers on Windows and Linux.

  • Proven experience with hardware triggering and synchronization of multiple devices (cameras, motion, lasers, DAQ).

  • Experience with FPGA development or working closely with FPGA-based timing hardware.

  • Solid grasp of hardware interfaces and networking: Ethernet, USB, serial, PCIe, and multi-device lab networks.

  • Comfortable in the lab: reading schematics, using an oscilloscope and logic analyzer, and debugging where hardware and software meet.

  • Experience with Git and collaborative code review.

  • Full professional proficiency in English.

We value judgment and ownership over a perfect match. If you recognize yourself in most of this, we would like to hear from you.

Bonus

  • Experience with machine-vision cameras, frame grabbers or high-throughput image acquisition.

  • Experience with precision motion controllers and encoder-based position triggering.

  • High-speed data paths to a host PC, SoC FPGAs or Linux driver development.

  • Experience building lightweight web or API layers for instrument control and live data.

  • Background in optics, lasers, coherent imaging, semiconductor metrology or lithography equipment.

  • Experience with CI, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or working in a Scrum team.

What we offer

  • Ownership of the embedded and timing backbone of a tool that does not exist anywhere else yet.

  • A small team with short feedback loops and real impact on the product.

  • Hands-on work at the meeting point of hardware, optics and software, on the High Tech Campus Eindhoven.

  • A competitive salary for the Dutch market.

title: Embedded Software Engineer - SoM
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Embedded Software Engineer at Harmattan AI, you will join the R&D team to own the embedded software stack on the compute modules used across our platforms. You will take a new module from bare board to a maintained, securely booting Linux platform, covering the boot chain, kernel, drivers, and the verification around them. This is a high impact role that combines deep Linux and kernel work with hands on bring up on new hardware, taking a board from first power up through to flight.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • BSP and Reference Images: Build and maintain the BSP layer, device trees, and the reference images for each board, including custom layers and SDK generation, and carry them forward across kernel upgrades and silicon revisions.

  • Boot Chain and Secure Boot: Own the boot chain, including bootloader porting, signed boot, verified rootfs, and A/B system update.

  • Drivers and Low Level Interfaces: Develop and validate Linux device drivers across I2C, SPI, UART, GPIO, PCIe, and MIPI, including camera and sensor interfaces.

  • Board Support on MCU Targets: Provide startup, clock, and peripheral support on the microcontrollers of boards the team designs.

  • Board Bring Up and Hardware Validation: Lead software bring up on new hardware, take part in design reviews, and debug system level issues across the hardware and software boundary.

  • Verification and Documentation: Define verification test plans and acceptance criteria, automate boot and peripheral test on real targets, and document each milestone.

  • Cross Functional Collaboration: Work with the hardware team on new boards, and with Systems and Embedded Software Platform on interfaces and integration.

  • Mentorship: Depending on seniority, mentor junior embedded engineers.

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

  • Educational Background: MSc in engineering (electrical, computer, or a related field). PhD a plus. A hands on bring up record matters more than the specific degree.

  • Experience: 5 years minimum in embedded software, with BSPs owned through their lifecycle and kept reproducible as the hardware evolved.

  • Build Systems: Strong command of an embedded Linux build system such as Yocto or OpenEmbedded, across custom layers or packages, BSP integration, image build, and SDK generation. Experience with in house or non standard build systems is an advantage.

  • Technical Expertise: Kernel space driver development on ARM targets, validated against real peripherals across I2C, SPI, UART, GPIO, PCIe, and MIPI. Device tree work on new boards and hardware revisions. Board bring up from first power up to a booting Linux image.

  • Boot and Update: Bootloader porting, kernel configuration, signed boot, and firmware update mechanisms on production hardware, with security conscious and deterministic engineering practice throughout.

  • Programming: Strong C and C++, including kernel space coding, and strong Python scripting skills, with solid version control practice (Git).

  • Debugging Expertise: Able to isolate whether a fault sits in the driver, the kernel configuration, or the board, using GDB, JTAG, OpenOCD, kernel tracing, ftrace, and perf.

  • Professional Attributes: Rigorous, structured, and systematic, able to work autonomously, unfazed by a board that will not boot. Excellent communication and documentation skills, able to present platform and test results to engineers and senior stakeholders.

  • Additional Skills: Bare metal or RTOS firmware on microcontroller targets, experience enabling hardware accelerators on embedded SoCs including VPU and NPU drivers and runtimes, familiarity with the perception or control workloads that run on the module, and UAS, drone, or defense experience are strong advantages.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission, vision, and ambitious growth plans, ready to go the extra mile to ensure operational excellence. Thrives in a fast paced environment where priorities shift and no task is too small.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

And through Legal Business, our journalistic title, we deliver independent news, analysis and commentary on the business of law and the strategy, performance and leadership of the world’s leading law firms.

We are a growing, multi-site organisation, with colleagues working across research, data, technology, product, journalism, commercial and events in London, Leeds and Bristol.

About the Role

 

Our new Enterprise AI Product Owner will own the adoption and value of AI in how Legal 500 works. You'll use our enterprise AI tools, with Microsoft Copilot and the wider Microsoft 365 AI capability as the main platform. You'll recommend what should be built or adopted and why, put governance in place where none yet exists, and make sure people across the business use the tools well.

This is a business-facing product role that starts from how the business works, not a technical build role. Copilot is the primary tool of choice, but you'll also oversee the other AI tools the business adopts.

 

What you'll do

You'll sit centrally within our People & Business Operations function, reporting to the Director of People & Business Operations. Your remit covers the whole of Legal 500, not a single department. You'll:

  • Own the roadmap and prioritised backlog for our enterprise AI opportunities, recommending what to build or adopt, what not to, and why. You'll write clear user stories and acceptance criteria and hold a consistent line with senior stakeholders when demand exceeds capacity.

  • Start every opportunity from the end-to-end business process. You'll walk business owners through how work gets done today, often where no SOPs exist, map the pain points, coach them through mapping a future-state process, and find where Copilot, other AI tools or workflow changes will make a measurable difference.

  • Personally configure, test and refine Copilot skills, agents and team workflows. You'll take ideas through proof of concept and pilot, then hand ownership of the output to the business owner.

  • Design, implement and enforce AI governance from the ground up. This includes owning the intake and review process for new use cases, agents and workflows, working alongside our Data Protection Officer, Information Security and IT Operations

  • Own our enterprise AI libraries: the register of approved tools and the libraries of approved agents, prompts, templates and shared workflows. You'll keep them curated, current and compliant, and avoid duplication between tools.

  • Design and deliver upskilling yourself, including training sessions, guides, clinics and self-serve resources. You'll also lead AI working groups and champion networks.

  • Spot common patterns across teams and bring them together on shared processes and solutions, so the same problem isn't solved many times.

  • Define and track adoption and value, such as usage, time saved, quality and user confidence. You'll maintain an AI benefits register, report progress to senior stakeholders and feed role impact into workforce planning.

  

What we're looking for

Essential

  • A process-led consulting approach, with a structured way of walking business owners through end-to-end processes, including where no SOPs existed

  • Proven experience of setting up AI governance from scratch and enforcing it. This includes owning an intake and review process and working with specialists such as a Data Protection Officer and IT Operations

  • Hands-on Microsoft Copilot experience: you've personally configured Copilot skills, agents or team workflows. Using Copilot, or overseeing someone else configuring it, isn't enough

  • Strong product management skills: setting priorities, writing user stories, running a backlog and managing senior stakeholders well

  • Experience of owning enterprise libraries or other centralised controls

  • Experience of running enablement yourself: you've designed and delivered upskilling personally, without relying on an L&D team, and you're comfortable leading working groups

 

Desirable

  • A genuine interest in enterprise efficiency and how people actually work, with a track record of bringing teams together on shared ways of working

  • A background in internal transformation, process improvement or Microsoft 365/Copilot SME roles, ideally including evaluating, onboarding or governing other enterprise AI tools

  • An understanding of professional services, publishing, legal markets or other knowledge-intensive environments

 

What this role isn't

  • It isn't about owning AI models in production, and working with development teams isn't the main job. There will be occasional technical work, but if you're mainly motivated by software delivery, this probably isn't the role for you

  • It isn't about running governance within someone else's framework, or handing enablement off to an L&D team. We need someone who has set these up and delivered them personally

 

Role information:

  • Hybrid workplace - 3 days a week in office, 2 days remote

  • This role can be based in either London or Leeds

  • Occasional travel to the other offices may be required (Bristol, London and Leeds)

title: Enterprise Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Enterprise Product Manager

The Role

Lyrebird is already trusted by thousands of clinicians, and the largest health organisations in Australia and the UK are now rolling it out across their entire workforce. This is a new role, created to lead the next chapter of our enterprise product as those deployments grow in size and ambition. You'll own the enterprise product end to end: the core platform capability that serves every enterprise customer, and the tailored work that deepens our partnership with specific ones. You'll have a real roadmap, a real engineering team, and the scope to shape where enterprise goes next.

A good week in this role might include a roadmap session with a state health service's IT team, a deep dive with a private hospital group to understand what's behind their latest request and how it could become something every enterprise customer benefits from, and a morning with engineering working out which of three competing priorities goes first. Your customers are the people deploying Lyrebird across their organisation, not the clinicians themselves, so you'll spend more time in customer conversations than most PMs do. If you enjoy that mix, and like being the person who makes the call when everything seems urgent, you'll do well here.

About Us

We turn real clinical conversations into accurate notes, automatically, backed by ambient real time document creation, intelligent document management and clinical workflow automation, native patient data integrations across siloed health systems, and a patient and clinical communications layer. Thousands of clinicians across multiple disciplines use Lyrebird every day in environments where accuracy, safety, and time matter deeply. We're growing fast across Melbourne, the UK, and Asia, and there's a finite window right now to set the standard for clinical AI in Australia before anyone else does.

What you'll do

  • Own the enterprise product, extending how Lyrebird serves hospitals, health services and multi-site groups: org hierarchy, SSO and provisioning, admin tooling, template governance, audit and usage reporting

  • Shape the enterprise roadmap, sequencing the platform capability that unlocks our next wave of large-scale deployments, and use it as a tool to communicate direction to customers, setting clear expectations about what's coming and when.

  • Build and own the prioritisation framework for enterprise, with clear, written criteria for core and tailored work that the whole business can rely on

  • Bring several independent streams of enterprise requests into one set of priorities, so every request has a clear home, a priority and a rationale anyone can explain

  • Turn tailored customer requests into buildable solutions, and spot the ones that are really core product needs wearing a customer's name

  • Stand up the voice-of-customer loop, spending real time with senior customer stakeholders and making sure what they tell you shapes what gets built

  • Drive roadmap decisions from usage and adoption data, working hand in hand with our UK team so every market benefits from what we learn

  • Deliver customer-specific integrations and workflows for some of the largest health organisations in the country, coordinating across engineering teams you don't own

What you'll bring

  • Experience owning a B2B or enterprise product end to end, shipped for large, complex organisations with their own governance, stakeholders and procurement

  • A track record of handling bespoke customer work without refusing it outright or letting it consume the roadmap, and the real examples to show how you made those calls

  • A habit of prioritising with written, defensible criteria, and the ability to walk through the trade-offs behind decisions you've made

  • Credibility in the room with senior enterprise customers: presenting and defending a roadmap to an executive or IT lead, and knowing when to hold the line and when to change course

  • The technical fluency to work credibly with engineers on architecture, integration and feasibility, and to land dependencies with teams that have their own roadmaps

Nice to have

  • Experience in health tech, clinical software or another regulated domain, including familiarity with EMRs and Australian health system structures such as LHDs, HHSs and private hospital groups

  • Hands-on experience building enterprise platform capability (SSO, provisioning, permissions, audit) or integration depth with HL7, FHIR and identity

  • An understanding of what hospital security, privacy and information-governance reviews demand of a vendor

  • Experience working across two markets with different regulatory requirements, or standing up a voice-of-customer loop from scratch

When a hospital rolls Lyrebird out to every clinician on every ward, the product has to work for the organisation as well as for the doctor in the room. The enterprise product is how thousands more clinicians spend their time on patients instead of paperwork, in the places where the pressure, and the risk of something being missed, is highest. That's the work.

We're building a team that reflects the diversity of the people who benefit from our work. We want Lyrebird to be a place where everyone feels safe, supported, and able to thrive. If you're from an underrepresented background in tech, we strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement.

descriptionHtml:
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Le contexte La squad Productivity est au cœur de la transformation produit autour de la gestion des affaires contentieuses de bout en bout. Le scope de la squad s'est considérablement enrichi, au-delà du seul gain de productivité, en allant vers l'accompagnement de la réflexion et de l'argumentation juridique, à travers plusieurs langues. Aujourd’hui, elle est responsable de toute la chaîne de valeur : 1. Analyse de documents 2. Rédaction automatisée des conclusions et documents juridiques 3. Réflexion stratégique sur l’argumentation C’est le cœur de notre IA appliquée au raisonnement juridique : travail avancé sur les modèles LLM, le machine learning et la structuration de documents complexes.1. Tu peux trouver des détails sur l’ensemble de la stack sur Github ! A savoir : il n’est pas nécessaire d’avoir une expérience professionnelle dans le domaine du droit, cependant l’envie de s’investir et de monter en compétence dans la compréhension des documents juridique est importante :)

  • Maintenir et faire évoluer notre architecture cloud — stack moderne, scalabilité, fiabilité des services en production.
  • Participer activement aux choix techniques de ta squad — revues de code, décisions d'architecture, amélioration continue de la qualité du code.

title: Expert Solution Architect, AI & Enterprise (all genders)
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

You'll own the path from a corporate client's business problem to a target architecture the CIO signs and the CFO funds. Not one platform, the whole picture: CRM, data, integrations, custom software, and the agentic AI layer on top. You'll lead discovery with enterprise clients, structure what they actually need, design the solution, defend it in the steering committee, and hand delivery a scope that holds. This is an Expert seat: the architecture benchmark of our Consulting Practice, no people management.

What You'll Do

  • Lead discovery and solution design on our enterprise engagements, turning ambiguous business problems into signed target architectures across CRM, data, custom software, and agentic AI

  • Own the architecture through delivery, so what you design in pre-sales is what gets built, without structural redesigns after signature

  • Scope six-figure engagements with estimates that hold, phasing that corporate procurement can sign, and risks named up front

  • Build the team's Solution Design Toolkit: discovery framework, architecture decision template, and an honest agentic-fit assessment that says where agents add value and where they don't

  • Present and defend architectures in front of CIOs, CFOs, and business unit heads, in German and English

  • Create reusable solution patterns (master data ownership between CRM and ERP, agent orchestration on HubSpot, data remediation before AI) that consultants and engineers actually use

  • Partner with our AI & Engineering Practice as the architecture counterpart: you own the solution design, they own the technical blueprint and the build

What You Bring

Must-haves

  • 6+ years in consulting or solution architecture, with at least 2 years personally owning solution design for enterprise clients on the advisory or vendor side, from discovery to signature

  • A track record of structuring ambiguous business problems into architecture options, scope, and risk, with artefacts you produced yourself and can walk us through

  • Architecture-level fluency across at least one enterprise CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, or Dynamics), one ERP (SAP or Dynamics), data platforms (warehouse, CDP, or MDM), and integration patterns (event-driven, API, iPaaS or middleware)

  • At least one AI or agentic solution you designed or delivered that ran in production for a client, with business outcomes you can name and failures you can explain

  • Experience leading conversations with CIO, CFO, procurement, IT security, and business stakeholders inside corporate groups, including telling an executive no with a case behind it

  • Commercial judgment on scoping and estimating engagements, and ownership when estimates miss

  • German and English at full business fluency, with the ability to present the same architecture to a CFO and to a delivery team

Nice-to-haves

  • Hands-on HubSpot enterprise experience or HubSpot Solutions Architect certification (we fund it if you don't have it)

  • Direct experience with EU AI Act and DSGVO as design constraints in regulated industries (manufacturing, financial services, healthcare)

  • A background in one of our core client sectors: industrial manufacturing, building products, or B2B distribution

  • Talks, articles, or teaching on enterprise architecture or applied AI

Your Team

You'll join the Strategy Consulting team within Thorit's Consulting Practice, which owns the strategy layer of our engagements. The Team Lead Strategy Consulting seat is currently open, so you'll report directly to the Practice Lead Consulting until it is filled. Day to day you'll work with our CRM Implementation and Managed Services teams, the Project Management Practice, and the AI & Engineering Practice in Böblingen and Lisbon, which builds what you design. Our company language is English.

Tech Stack

  • Core: HubSpot (CRM, Marketing, Sales, Service, Operations Hub), Jira, Confluence, Forecast, Claude AI

  • Architecture & design: architecture decision records, C4 and sequence diagrams, Miro

  • Enterprise landscape you design against: SAP S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Salesforce, data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery), CDP and MDM concepts, iPaaS and custom middleware

  • AI & agents: LLM-based agents on Claude and other models, retrieval, orchestration frameworks, evaluation and guardrails; the engineering team builds with Claude Code and Cursor

What We Offer

  • 31 days of paid vacation: 30 days plus one additional company day each year, well above the German statutory minimum of 20

  • Company pension (Allianz): employer contribution from your second year, rising with tenure from €50 to €290 per month

  • Lunch allowance: €5 tax-free per working day via Lunchit, up to €100 per month, usable anywhere

  • Business Bike: bicycle leasing through payroll with full insurance and free brand choice

  • Corporate Benefits: discounts across several hundred brands for private use

  • Hybrid Flex model: two office days per week at our Böblingen HQ, the rest where you work best

  • Real ownership: direct client leadership on enterprise engagements, and a Practice that builds and operates agentic systems rather than presenting them

About Thorit

title: Facilities Readiness Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

The role

As Facilities Readiness Lead, you will set the standard for when a Volta facility is ready to receive network and compute. You will own the readiness criteria and release process that every DSX site uses to hand space over for installation and turn-up.

This is an expert-level individual contributor role. Reporting to the Senior Director, Global Commissioning & Handover, you will set direction across construction, commissioning, operations and deployment teams, and your recommendation will decide whether an area is released, conditionally released or held.

What you will do

Readiness standard

  • Own Volta's global facilities readiness standard: criteria, evidence, approvals and release process by building, hall or zone.

  • Set the governance for readiness decisions and exceptions across all sites.

  • Set requirements for access, safety, fire protection, housekeeping and temporary arrangements in live and phased sites.

Release decisions

  • Recommend release, conditional release or deferral to delivery leadership, and escalate readiness risks early.

  • Align readiness with GPU deployment, network delivery and turn-up dates.

  • Make sure asset information, drawings and operating instructions reach receiving teams.

Improvement

  • Use deployment lessons to evolve the standard.

What we are looking for

  • Expert-level experience in data centre construction, commissioning, facilities engineering or technical handover, typically 9 to 12 years.

  • A track record setting readiness or acceptance processes across multiple sites or teams.

  • Strong understanding of power, cooling, controls and physical infrastructure dependencies.

  • Sound judgement on readiness risk and confidence making release calls with senior stakeholders.

  • Ability to drive multiple disciplines to closure without direct authority.

Nice to have

  • Releasing facilities for high-density GPU installations.

  • Phased delivery in live or partially operational sites.

  • Repeatable acceptance processes across a portfolio.

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.
As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

  • Competitive salary based on the work you do here, not your previous salary

  • Equity in Volta, giving you the opportunity to share in the company's long-term success

  • Retirement/pension contributions

  • Comprehensive health, wellbeing and insurance benefits

  • Generous number of vacation days each year

Additional Information

Background Checks

All offers of employment at Volta are conditional on the satisfactory completion of pre-employment screening, which includes confirmation of your right to work, verification of your employment history and a criminal record check, where this is permitted by local law. Screening is carried out by Zinc, an accredited third-party provider, after an offer is made and all information is handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable data protection law.

Equal Opportunity

Volta is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and make employment decisions based on skills, qualifications, experience and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Accessibility

Volta is committed to providing an accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. If you require accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the application or interview process, please contact us at

Candidate Privacy Notice

By applying, you consent to the processing of your personal data for recruitment purposes in accordance with applicable data protection laws, including the UK GDPR, EU GDPR and relevant US state privacy regulations. Your data will be shared only with those involved in the hiring process and will not be used for unrelated purposes. For details, see our Recruitment & Candidate Privacy Notice.

Note to Recruitment Agencies

Volta does not accept unsolicited CVs or candidate profiles from recruitment agencies. Any unsolicited submissions, including those sent directly to hiring managers or employees, will be treated as the property of Volta. No agency fees will be payable unless a valid, signed recruitment agreement is in place, and the agency has been specifically engaged for the relevant vacancy.
